q: What's the time window for calling a stroke alert?
answer_quote: Patient will be considered a Stroke Alert Patient if the Time Last Known Well is within twenty-four (24) hours

q: What are the G.F.A.S.T. stroke screening items and how is each scored?
answer_quote: G Gaze Abnormalities (0-1) F Facial Asymmetry (0-1) A Arm or leg Weakness/Drift (0-1) S Speech Difficulties (0-1) T Time Last Known Well (no point)
note: The quote is the G.F.A.S.T. box in reading order, with the correct rendered spelling. The PDF text layer has glyph errors here: 'Abnormali.es', 'Weakness/Dri9', 'Diﬃcul.es' (see sections_key.jsonl box_item rows). A parser that copies those errors should not get exact-match credit.

q: GFAST score is 4. Where do I take the patient?
answer_quote: If patient has four (4) points on the G.F.A.S.T stroke screening transport the patient to a Comprehensive Stroke Center (Policy 602).

q: GFAST 4, but the nearest Comprehensive Stroke Center is about an hour away. Where do I go?
answer_quote: If transport time to closest Comprehensive Stroke Center is greater than forty-five (45) minutes, transport to the closest Primary Stroke Center.
note: The flowchart on page 3 disagrees on the NO branch: it says 'Transport to closest Stroke Center'. The section text is the answer (see flowchart_700a13_key.json).

q: Patient has a GFAST of 2. Which hospital should they go to?
answer_quote: If patient has three (3) or fewer points on the G.F.A.S.T stroke screening transport the patient to the closest Stroke Center (Comprehensive or Primary) (Policy 602).

q: Last known well was 30 hours ago. What does the stroke flowchart say to do?
answer_quote: Continue routine medical care
note: The answer is in the raster flowchart image only (node n3, edge 'More than 24 hours'). There is no text layer for it, so the parser needs OCR or vision.

q: What does the destination policy say if the Comprehensive Stroke Center is more than 45 minutes away?
answer_quote: If the transport time to the closest Comprehensive Stroke Center is greater than forty-five (45) minutes, transport to the closest Primary Stroke Center in accordance with Section (F)(2) of this policy.
note: Physical page 15 is in the clean copy of Policy 602. Page 5 (the redline copy) has identical text. The '(F)(2)' cross-reference is printed that way, although F is STEMI and the Primary Stroke rule is E.2.

q: Do I need to check a blood sugar on a suspected stroke?
answer_quote: Determine Blood Glucose Level (BGL) (700-A03)

q: Suspected stroke patient, glucose is 48. Which protocol do I switch to?
answer_quote: Blood Glucose Level (BGL), if less than 60 mg/dL see Protocol (700-A03)

q: At what glucose reading does hypoglycemia need treatment under routine medical care?
answer_quote: Readings of less than 60 mg/dl along with symptoms of hypoglycemia or altered mental status requires intervention (700-A03)

q: Patient had a seizure when the stroke symptoms started. Is it still a stroke alert?
answer_quote: If patient has had a seizure during the duration of stroke symptoms or is actively seizing, see (700-A02) and transport to appropriate Emergency Department.

q: How should I position a suspected stroke patient?
answer_quote: Place patient in supine position with head elevated 30 degrees

q: Patient woke up with stroke symptoms. What time do I document as last known well?
answer_quote: If patient was last known well prior to bedtime, this is the time to be documented, not the time they woke up with symptoms present

q: What should I get from the family before leaving on a stroke call?
answer_quote: Collect contact number for a reliable historian that can state the patient’s “Time Last Known Well” and medical history.

q: What demographics go at the start of a hospital radio report?
answer_quote: a. Unit ID (agency, type, number) b. Estimated Time of Arrival c. Patient’s Age d. Patient’s Sex

q: How does a Stroke Alert radio report have to start?
answer_quote: specialty center radio reports shall start with a clear statement indicating what type of alert applies to the patient (Trauma Alert, Stroke Alert, or STEMI Alert)

q: Do I call in a stroke alert by cell phone or by radio?
answer_quote: Trauma Alerts, STEMI Alerts, Stroke Alerts, and critical patient transports, transporting with red lights and sirens (RLS), to the hospital shall be transmitted via self-initiated radio on the designated hospital ringdown channel.

q: When should the stroke specialty-center radio report be given?
answer_quote: Specialty center hospital reports should occur prior to departure from the scene

q: Which hospitals are Comprehensive Stroke Centers?
answer_quote: Comprehensive Stroke Center: ECH, GSH, KSC, RSJ, SUH
answer_set_full_names: El Camino Hospital of Mountain View
Regional Medical Center of San Jose

q: Which hospitals are Primary Stroke Centers?
answer_quote: Primary Stroke Center: ECH, GSH, KSC, LGH, OCH, RSJ, SLH, STH, SUH, VMC
answer_set_full_names: El Camino Hospital of Mountain View
El Camino Hospital of Los Gatos
Regional Medical Center of San Jose

q: Is Valley Medical Center a Comprehensive Stroke Center?
answer_quote: Comprehensive Stroke Center: VMC not checked (VMC is checked for Primary Stroke Center)
note: Checks that a parser reads an EMPTY cell correctly. Expected answer: no, VMC is a Primary Stroke Center only.

q: What's the difference between a Primary and a Comprehensive Stroke Center?
answer_quote: Comprehensive Stroke Center (CSC) means a hospital with specific abilities to receive, diagnose and treat all stroke cases and provide the highest level of care for stroke patients.
note: The companion definition is III.A.1 on page 1: 'Primary Stroke Center (PSC) means a hospital that treats acute stroke patients, and identified patients who may benefit from transfer to a higher level of care when clinically warranted.'

q: What's the tPA (alteplase) dose for an ischemic stroke?
note: None of the five documents mention thrombolytics (tPA, alteplase, tenecteplase, fibrinolytic, lytic). Checked with grep on every text layer.

q: What blood pressure should I treat to in a suspected stroke patient?
note: Near miss. 700-S04 covers how to measure blood pressure (2.3, 2.3.1) and a morphine SBP threshold (6.4.1), and 605 gives trauma-triage SBP cut-offs, but no document gives a stroke blood-pressure target or treatment threshold.

q: What radio channel is the Good Samaritan ringdown on?
note: Near miss. Policy 501 (II.C, IV.B) says only 'the designated hospital ringdown channel'. No channel, frequency or talkgroup is listed anywhere.

q: When do I give the hospital a heads-up that I'm bringing in a possible sepsis patient?
answer_quote: Advanced notification to hospital of suspected sepsis patient if two or more SIRS criteria are met

q: Does a low end-tidal CO2 count toward sepsis, and what's the cutoff?
answer_quote: ETCO2 less than 25 mmHg

q: What blood pressure am I trying to hold in a septic patient?
answer_quote: Maintain systolic blood pressure greater than 90 mmHg to ensure adequate perfusion

q: Shock patient, I've given the first saline bolus and the lungs still sound clear. Can I give another one?
answer_quote: May repeat once if lung sounds remain clear

q: My trauma patient is a trauma alert. What am I allowed to do on scene before we leave?
answer_quote: If patient is a Trauma Alert Patient all BLS and ALS care except for airway management and spinal motion restriction is to be completed en route to the selected Trauma Center

q: What scene time should I aim for with an unstable trauma patient?
answer_quote: Target scene time less than 10 minutes for unstable patients or those likely to need surgical intervention

q: The injury happened four hours ago. Is the patient still inside the window for TXA?
answer_quote: Injury is less than 3 hours old

q: Adult fell about 12 feet off a roof but looks okay. Is that a trauma alert?
answer_quote: Fall from height > 10 feet (all ages)

q: 70-year-old trauma patient with a systolic of 104. Does that make them a trauma alert?
answer_quote: Age older than 65 years: Systolic BP is less than 110 mmHg

q: Where do major burn patients get transported?
answer_quote: Transport all identified major burn patients to a designated burn center

q: How fast do I need the 12-lead on a chest pain patient?
answer_quote: 12-lead ECG obtained within 10 minutes of patient contact

q: Monitor says Acute MI Suspected but we're still far from the hospital. When do I send the 12-lead?
answer_quote: Transmit 12 Lead ECG to the selected STEMI Center, when the first transmission capable monitor arrives, regardless of ETA to receiving facility

q: Do I have to chart when the aspirin was given on a chest pain call?
answer_quote: Time of aspirin administration

q: Chest pain patient took Viagra last night. Can he still get nitro?
answer_quote: To avoid hypotension, withhold nitroglycerin if patient has taken phosphodiesterase inhibitor within the past 48 hours.

q: How much ST elevation counts as a STEMI on the 12-lead?
answer_quote: The criteria for ST elevation is at least 1mm ST segment elevation in inferior lead, or at least a 2mm ST segment elevation in anterior or lateral leads, or 2 or more contiguous leads.

q: Overdose patient swallowed an unknown amount of pills and has no gag reflex. Can I give activated charcoal?
answer_quote: Charcoal is contraindicated if patient lacks gag reflex and cannot self-administer

q: Tricyclic overdose: at what QRS width does the protocol call for sodium bicarb?
answer_quote: a QRS widening greater than 0.10 seconds

q: Elderly lady fell four days ago, no red criteria. Do I still need to call a trauma alert?
answer_quote: If patient fell more than 72 hours ago and does not meet any “Red” Prehospital Trauma Triage criteria, activation as Trauma Alert Patient is not required

q: Ground-level fall with a possible hip fracture, no trauma alert criteria. Where can I take her?
answer_quote: Suspected hip fractures not meeting trauma alert criteria can be transported to closest ED for evaluation

q: Lift assist, the patient isn't going to the hospital. What should I tell the family before we leave?
answer_quote: Encourage a caregiver to remain with patient and monitor for changes in neurological status for at least 24 hours

q: The tourniquet has been on for more than two hours. Can I loosen it?
answer_quote: If a tourniquet has been placed for over two (2) hours, the provider may elect to slowly back off the tourniquet every five (5) minutes.

q: Where exactly should the tourniquet go on the limb?
answer_quote: Windlass tourniquets shall be placed proximal to the wound, not over a joint and in accordance to manufacturers specifications.

q: Stab wound to the belly that I can't compress. What's the priority?
answer_quote: Rapid transport to surgical intervention is the priority for these patients.

q: How big is the fluid bolus for a child in shock?
answer_quote: Infant and Child: 20 ml/kg Normal Saline IV/IO, max of 60 ml/kg

q: Kid pulled from a pool in cardiac arrest, possible neck injury. Which hospital?
answer_quote: Any drowning or mechanical asphyxiation patient, in cardiac arrest, with suspected head or spinal injury shall be transported to a Pediatric Trauma Center (Policy 602)

q: When does a child's seizure count as status epilepticus?
answer_quote: Identify Status Epilepticus characterized by continuous seizure lasting more than 5 minutes OR more than one seizure without return to baseline mental status

q: What systolic pressure is too low for a 5-year-old?
answer_quote: ≥ 4 yr – 6 yr >140 >34 <70 + (age in yr x 2)

q: We got ROSC on a child in medical arrest. Where do we transport?
answer_quote: Transport to closest Advanced Pediatric Receiving Center, unless a traumatic cardiac arrest

q: What blood sugar counts as hypoglycemia in a newborn?
answer_quote: If BGL is less than 60mg/dl or less than 45mg/dl for neonates administer:

q: Do the 12-lead tracings have to go into the ePCR?
answer_quote: 12 Lead ECG waveforms, regardless of the monitor interpretation.

q: What's the ketamine dose for pain in an adult trauma patient?
note: None of the indexed documents mention ketamine. Near miss: 700-A16 3.5 sends pain management to 700-S04, which covers other analgesics.

q: What CPAP pressure do I start at for a CHF patient?
note: Near miss: 700-S04 4.4 says only 'CPAP is defined under 700-M12' (700-M12 is not in the archive) and Policy 302 lists the CPAP device in the inventory. No pressure setting appears anywhere.

q: Adult in cardiac arrest, no ROSC after 20 minutes of CPR. Can we stop resuscitation?
note: The adult cardiac arrest protocol 700-A07 is not indexed: only its superseded 2025 copy is in archive/previous/. Near miss: 700-P07 5.2 gives the pediatric termination rule, which does not answer an adult question.

q: What's the cyanide antidote for a smoke inhalation patient?
note: No indexed document mentions cyanide or hydroxocobalamin. Near miss: 700-A15 covers organophosphates (ATNAA) and other toxins.
